## Highlights

Zova 1.5.0 makes the browser package a stable 1.x surface and brings every
language binding up to the complete C ABI. `zova-wasm` now covers transactions,
streaming objects, filtered vector search, maintenance, persistent-database
management, extensions and in-place migration, and is qualified in Chromium and
Firefox. The key-value store gains ordered scans and compare-and-swap, and
objects can be stored with per-chunk LZ4 compression. Storage moves to format
14, so databases written by 1.4.0 need one explicit `zova migrate` before 1.5.0
opens them. Go modules now ship prebuilt libraries, so `go get` alone builds.

## What's changed

### Browser package (zova-wasm)

- `zova-wasm` is now a stable 1.x surface, documented in the new "Browser
  package (zova-wasm)" section of `API_STABILITY.md`: calls, errors, the OPFS
  storage and ownership contract, supported browsers, and the named differences
  from native `zova-js`. A reviewed declaration snapshot and a parity table that
  lists every public `zova-js` name are checked in `bun run test`.
- **Breaking:** errors now use the native `zova-js` fields. `ZovaError.code` is
  the status name (for example `"ZOVA_CONSTRAINT"`) and `status` is its number.
  Before, `status` held the name and `statusCode` the number. `statusCode` and
  `ZovaWasmError` remain as deprecated aliases, but code that reads
  `error.status` as a name must switch to `error.code`.
- Native SQL, transaction, KV and notification APIs: `begin`, `commit`,
  `rollback` and savepoints, statement stepping with bindings, KV batches and
  namespaces, and `notify`/`listen`.
- Streaming objects: `objectWriter` as a `WritableStream`, `objectReader` as a
  `ReadableStream` of verified reads, `objectSeekableReader` for range serving,
  and the chunk and manifest APIs. The browser build commits object chunks in
  4 MiB batches because a worker's WebAssembly memory never shrinks.
- Filtered vector search with the native `VectorSearchOptions`
  (`candidateIds`, `maxDistance`), and multi-vector int8 search.
- Maintenance in browsers: `reclaimSpace`, `vacuum`, verified `backupTo` and
  `compactTo`, and `restoreBackup`, with progress phases and `AbortSignal`
  cancellation. A stopped worker never leaves a partial target.
- Persistent-database management: `listPersistent`, `deletePersistent`,
  streamed `exportStream` and `importPersistent`. Streaming a 1.16 GB database
  through export and import kept worker memory under 27 MB.
- In-place migration of persistent databases with `probePersistent` and
  `migratePersistent`. Opening still never migrates. An interrupted migration
  leaves either the original or the migrated database.
- Extensions: the bundled `trgm` extension, and plugins linked statically into
  a custom module through `ZOVA_WASM_PLUGIN_SOURCES`.
- Every other browser-applicable C ABI function: KV scans and compare-and-swap,
  `setObjectCompression`, opaque-key graph APIs, graph scans and directional
  walks, fresh-build sessions, and `registerFunction` for SQL functions
  implemented as worker modules.
- Qualified browsers: Chromium-based desktop browsers 149 and later, and desktop
  Firefox 155 and later. Safari, WebKit, mobile and private browsing are not
  qualified.

### Language bindings

- The safe Rust crate, Go, Python and JavaScript (synchronous `Database`) now
  wrap every function declared in `include/zova.h`. Newly reachable without raw
  FFI: opaque-key graph APIs, keyed fresh graph builds, fresh-build sessions,
  multi-vector int8 search, scalar SQL functions implemented in the host
  language, statically linked plugins, extension upgrade and rebuild, bundle
  verify/trust/untrust, and create options.
- `scripts/check-abi-coverage.py` fails CI when a binding neither references a
  C ABI function nor lists it with a reason in
  `scripts/abi-coverage-allowlist.json`.

### Key-value store

- Ordered scans in byte order with an optional prefix, start and end bounds, a
  continuation key, a limit and a keys-only mode. Bounds reduce to one
  primary-key range read.
- `put if absent`, `compare and put` and `compare and delete` apply only when
  the stored state matches, are operation-atomic inside caller transactions,
  and report whether they applied.
- Available in Zig, through `zova_kv_scan`, `zova_kv_put_if_absent`,
  `zova_kv_compare_and_put` and `zova_kv_compare_and_delete`, and in every
  binding.

### Objects

- Opt-in per-chunk LZ4 compression. A chunk is stored compressed only when that
  makes it smaller; chunk hashes, object ids, manifests and deduplication are
  unchanged. Compression is a per-handle setting, off by default:
  `Database.setObjectCompression`, `zova_object_set_compression`, and every
  binding. With LZ4, log-like text was 2.2-2.8x smaller at 2-19% lower ingest
  and 8-17% lower read throughput; with compression off, throughput is
  unchanged (`bench/object_compression_227.md`).

### Go

- Released Go module versions carry `zova.h` and a prebuilt `libzova_c.a` for
  linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64 and windows/amd64
  (MinGW), so `go get` alone builds; cgo still needs a C compiler. The
  `zova_external` build tag selects another build through `CGO_CFLAGS` and
  `CGO_LDFLAGS`.
- The released module is about 33 MB to download.

### Documentation and testing

- New `docs/concurrency.md`: a recommended setup for one writer handle and
  several reader handles, what readers see in WAL and rollback-journal modes,
  and why rollback-journal mode is recommended when transactions must stay
  consistent across bound-store files.
- Fuzz targets for LZ4 decoding, encoded-vector validation, extension bundle
  manifests, and the CLI inspection, doctor and salvage commands over damaged
  databases. Their corpora replay in the normal test suites;
  `zig build fuzz --fuzz=<runs>` and a manual workflow search for new inputs.
  CI builds the generated C under AddressSanitizer and
  UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.
- Zig and Go are now tested on Windows in CI.
- Fixed `zova info`, `stats`, `objects`, `chunks` and `salvage` crashing on a
  damaged database with a negative stored object or chunk size. They now report
  `ObjectCorrupt` or `VectorCorrupt`. Two error-path leaks in the inspect
  loaders are also fixed.
- `trgm` salvage now skips a source row that violates a destination constraint
  instead of failing the salvage.
- Checking the `trgm` extension no longer takes time quadratic in the number of
  indexed documents: 2,000 documents took 15.8 s and now take 0.19 s.
- Plugin table operations no longer prepare snapshot statements for every row,
  which was about 8.5 µs per row and is now about 50 ns.
- `zova migrate --dry-run` reports destination free space on Windows.

## Compatibility

- Package and C ABI identity are `1.5.0`. The C ABI change is additive; code
  built against 1.4.0 keeps working. No status codes were added.
- Storage format is now 14. Open never migrates silently: format 9, 10, 11, 12
  and 13 databases are reported as migration-required and left unchanged.
  Migrate them with `zova migrate` or the `migrate` call in any binding;
  migrated chunks stay uncompressed. Zova 1.4.0 and earlier cannot open
  format-14 files, and downgrades are unsupported.
- `zova-wasm` joins the 1.x commitment with the named browser exceptions in
  `API_STABILITY.md`. Its error fields changed as described above.
- The plugin ABI stays at v1. No new plugin operations were added.
- Existing 1.x ownership, ordering, error, and transaction guarantees remain in
  force.

## Installation and distribution

- Native packages use `1.5.0` across Cargo, PyPI, npm, and Go.
- Python publishes CPython 3.13 stable-ABI wheels tested on Python 3.13 and
  3.14; no Python source distribution is published.
- npm publishes `zova-js`, its native companion packages, and `zova-wasm`.
- Go's module tag is `bindings/go/v1.5.0`. It points at a child of the release
  commit that adds the prebuilt libraries; the release commit itself carries no
  binaries.

## Known boundaries

The browser package does not support run-time `.zovaext` bundles, a trust
store or `LinkedPlugin`, and cannot migrate a database with bound stores. One
browser connection owns a persistent name at a time. A seekable or partial
range read verifies each chunk it returns, not the whole-object hash. Core
vector search remains exact; approximate search is available only through the
experimental USearch reference extension. Extension authoring beyond the
documented common C ABI and the reference extensions remains experimental and
outside the stable native 1.x compatibility commitment.

**Full Changelog:** https://github.com/ata-sesli/zova/compare/v1.4.0...v1.5.0
